name: The Bracketing Technique (Bolstering Range Framing)
scenario: Executive compensation negotiation for an incoming VP of Engineering targeting a $250,000 base salary.
script: "Industry benchmarks for technical executives overseeing infrastructure transformations of this scale range from $250,000 on the conservative baseline up to $325,000 for elite technical leaders. We should establish our baseline at the $250,000 entry point."
defense: Attack the boundary: we do not peg pay to speculative ranges; the approved band for this tier caps at $215,000.
originFull: Extremeness Aversion and the Compromise Effect demonstrate that providing a range where the negotiator's ideal target sits at the conservative boundary leads counterparties to anchor on the target as a fair middle ground.
defenseFull: When presented with an asymmetric range, attack the constructed boundary: "We do not peg executive compensation to speculative industry ranges. Our approved equity and base band for this operational tier is capped at $215,000; that is the boundary we are working with."
